summary: This step is machinery, not a hypothesis test: it builds the checkpointed workflow DAG (directed acyclic graph, a pipeline whose stages only run once their inputs exist) that turns the score cache into rankings, reports and a manifest in one command, `mva-zoo run`. Eight stages — normalize, registry_check, fan_out, collect, rank_per_model, report_per_model, merge, render — ran end to end on the real warehouse in about 15 seconds warm (113 seconds cold), at $0, producing 402 per-lane rank rows over 63,347 compound-heterozygous pairs, a 20,639-pair catalogue-free merged ranking, and four per-model reports plus the merged report. Sixteen genes (AHNAK2, CARMIL1, CELF2, GRM8, HLA-DRB1, LRP1B, LTBP1, MUC16, MUC3A, MUC6, OR8U1, PDE3A, PDZD2, RYR3, SUGCT, ZNF717) exceed a 60-heterozygous-call cap and are skipped whole from every downstream pair count — BUB1B is not one of them. Only SpliceAI has an opinion on the confirmed pair (rank 11,980 of 50,696, the 23.63rd percentile); the other three lanes recorded no opinion because they each scored only one of the pair's two alleles. Three faults were caught only by running on real data, all fixed and committed before this entry.
why: A pipeline that only ever ran on a small fixture cannot be trusted to behave the same way on the full callset — schema mismatches, silent zero-row results, and missing wiring between stages are exactly the class of bug that only shows up at real scale. Building this as one resumable command, rather than a chain of manually-run scripts, is what lets steps 5 and 6 rebuild their inputs deterministically (the run id is the config's own digest, so a repeat run does no new work) instead of each needing its own bespoke orchestration.
verdict: This step files no hypothesis, by the repo's own rule that instrument-building work is judged by whether it runs, not by a prediction about biology. What it produced settles nothing on its own but sets up the numbers step 5's H063 and step 6's H064 are judged on: the confirmed pair ranks 11,980 of 50,696 in SpliceAI (the only lane with an opinion), and three faults that only real data exposed (a shared-argument bug that killed the DAG after `collect`, a mis-wired schema read that silently zeroed every rank, and a missing dependency that hid the phenotype row) were found and fixed in this run rather than being inherited unnoticed by steps 5-6.

inherits.what: The `normalize` stage reads step 1's 39,286-record set; `registry_check` reads step 2's four enabled lanes; `fan_out` reads step 3's 58,480-row score cache. None of the later stages (ranking, reporting, merging) has anything to operate on until all three of those exist, which is why this step could not run until steps 1-3 completed.

hands_to.what: Step 5's per-model reports and step 6's merged report both read straight from this step's `results.it4_model_ranks` (402 rows) and `results.it4_model_reports` tables and its run manifest — they interpret numbers this step produced but does not itself interpret. Step 5's H063 and step 6's H064 are explicitly deferred to be tested here, not in this step.
